title: Microsoft 365 Backup: Teams channel backup and recovery
summary: Hold: the listed Graph call enables Backup Storage rather than configuring backup policies. The briefing also incorrectly equates Teams' planned 30-day retention with existing workloads and presents undocumented Teams restore permissions and destinations as established capabilities.

claims.claim: This briefing concerns the Microsoft 365 Teams Channel Backup roadmap item.
claims.quote: "id": 570668, "title": "Microsoft 365: Teams Channel Backup"

claims.claim: The feature is in development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Targeted Release.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Targeted Release"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists December CY2026 as its target.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: No preview date is given.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the listed cloud.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: Other clouds are excluded from the Teams channel backup release.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Teams Channel Backup 570668 GCC Worldwide availability. Read roadmap record and backup-setup, backup-overview and backup-whats-new; none explicitly excludes other clouds for this feature.
claims.fix: Replace 'worldwide only' with 'with Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) listed on the roadmap; other clouds are not stated'.

claims.claim: Web is the listed platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The listed products are Microsoft 365 and Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft 365", "Microsoft 365 admin center"]

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The planned feature recovers team and channel data to a previously known good state after accidental changes or compromise.
claims.quote: A backup and recovery feature that lets you recover team & channel data (like files, messages exchanged over channels) in Microsoft Teams to a previously known good state after accidental changes or security compromises.

claims.claim: Files are included in the planned recoverable data.
claims.quote: team & channel data (like files, messages exchanged over channels)

claims.claim: Channel messages are included in the planned recoverable data.
claims.quote: team & channel data (like files, messages exchanged over channels)

claims.claim: The roadmap names Team and Channels (Standard, Private, Public), not shared channels.
claims.quote: Supported items include Team, Channels (Standard, Private, Public) and underlying data.

claims.claim: Shared channels are included, although the Scope and Open questions sections say their coverage is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: What's changing: 'standard, private and shared channels'. Scope: 'standard, private, public per the roadmap; shared channels not named'. Open questions: 'Whether chats, meeting recordings and shared channels are included.'
claims.fix: In What's changing, replace 'standard, private and shared channels' with 'standard, private and public channels, using the roadmap's wording'. Leave shared-channel coverage as an open question.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The planned supported retention period is 30 days.
claims.quote: Retention period supported is 30 days.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not establish whether chats or meeting content are covered.
claims.quote: Supported items include Team, Channels (Standard, Private, Public) and underlying data.

claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 Backup workloads include OneDrive accounts, SharePoint sites and Exchange mailboxes.
claims.quote: With the ability to back up all or select SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Exchange mailboxes, Microsoft 365 Backup provides comprehensive coverage for your critical data.

claims.claim: Existing workloads have frequent restore points.
claims.quote: For full account restores: 10 minutes for two weeks prior

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup provides fast restores through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: This is what the Microsoft 365 Backup product offers, both through the Microsoft 365 admin center, and via partner applications built on the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage platform.

claims.claim: Purview retention can preserve Teams messages.
claims.quote: You can use a retention policy to retain data from chats and channel messages in Teams, and delete these chats and messages.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention-policies-teams to sources.

claims.where: Why it matters: parenthesis about Purview retention
claims.claim: Purview retention does not restore Teams structure.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams deleted channel restore retention Purview retention policies structure restore. Read learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention-policies-teams and searched its text for restore and structure; no passage states this structural-restore limitation.
claims.fix: Replace 'which preserves but does not restore structure' with 'which preserves compliance copies searchable through eDiscovery', citing https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention-policies-teams.

claims.where: Why it matters: only safety nets
claims.claim: Purview retention and SharePoint recycle bins are the only existing safety nets for Teams channels.
claims.quote: Deleted shared channel can be restored within 30 days after deletion. When a deleted shared channel is restored, all previous memberships (individual and team sharing) will be restored.
claims.fix: Remove 'the only safety nets' assertion. Distinguish the planned point-in-time recovery from existing deleted-channel and deleted-team recovery documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/shared-channels.

claims.where: Why it matters: no clean recovery path
claims.claim: Deleting channels has had no clean recovery path.
claims.quote: Deleted teams can be restored within 30 days after deletion. When a team is deleted, all shared channels will also be deleted. When a deleted team is restored, all shared channels are restored as well with all sharing relationships.
claims.fix: Remove the categorical 'has had no clean recovery path' sentence. Say that the roadmap proposes recovery to a previously known good state, rather than implying that existing deleted-channel recovery is unavailable.

claims.claim: The Teams 30-day window matches the rest of Microsoft 365 Backup.
claims.quote: SharePoint and OneDrive backup policies now support recovery windows of 3 months, 6 months, or any whole number of years from 1 through 10. Exchange options remain 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, or 2 years. The existing one-year default is unchanged.
claims.fix: Delete 'and the 30-day window matches the rest of Microsoft 365 Backup'. Existing workloads have configurable recovery windows with a one-year default, not a 30-day window.

claims.claim: Restoration can bring back deleted content.
claims.quote: Full Exchange mailbox item restores or granular item restores using search, for modified or fully deleted items.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup data stays inside the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary.
claims.quote: Data never leaves the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary and honors the geographic locations of your current data residency.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup honors the tenant's data geography.
claims.quote: Data never leaves the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary and honors the geographic locations of your current data residency.

claims.claim: Multi-geo backup is supported for existing workloads.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup supports the backup of sites and user accounts from both the central and satellite locations.

claims.claim: SharePoint Administrators will be able to overwrite live Teams channel content through restore.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel backup default admin opt in roles SharePoint Administrator restore destination new location. Read backup-setup and backup-restore-data; the documented role matrix has OneDrive, SharePoint and Exchange, not Teams.
claims.fix: Remove the Teams-specific SharePoint Administrator restore assignment. State that Teams backup and restore role mappings are not yet documented; the existing matrix covers OneDrive, SharePoint and Exchange.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup Administrators will manage Teams policies and overwrite channel content through restore.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel backup default admin opt in roles SharePoint Administrator restore destination new location. Read backup-setup and backup-restore-data; neither provides a Teams backup or restore role mapping.
claims.fix: Qualify Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator permissions as background for currently documented workloads. Say that Teams backup and restore roles are not yet documented.

claims.claim: Departmental billing can confine administrators' backup management to subscriptions they are authorized to use.
claims.quote: This way only an approved admin who is given spending power on a subscription can create and edit backups and cause consumption to the department's Azure subscription.
claims.fix: Specify that the restriction covers backup-policy creation and editing through Azure Owner or Contributor permissions, not all restore authority. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-billing to sources.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams channel restoration supports an in-place operation that replaces current content.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel backup default admin opt in roles SharePoint Administrator restore destination new location. Read backup-restore-data and searched its text for Teams; overwrite workflows describe existing workloads only.
claims.fix: Make the Teams overwrite warning conditional: 'When Teams restore options are documented, confirm whether an in-place restore overwrites current content and agree the required compliance check.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A team can be restored to a new location without overwriting existing content.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel backup default admin opt in roles SharePoint Administrator restore destination new location. Read backup-restore-data and backup-whats-new; neither documents a Teams new-location restore.
claims.fix: Replace the new-location assertion and test instruction with 'When Teams restore destinations are documented, test a supported destination and record overwrite behavior'. Add Teams restore destinations to Open questions.

claims.claim: Restoring Teams content to a new location changes its links.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel backup default admin opt in roles SharePoint Administrator restore destination new location. Read backup-restore-data; new URLs are described for OneDrive and SharePoint, not Teams.
claims.fix: Remove the asserted Teams link behavior. Ask administrators to document link behavior when testing whatever Teams restore destinations Microsoft eventually documents.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup uses consumption-based pay-as-you-go billing rather than user-based licensing.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup is a pay-as-you-go offering that charges based on consumption, unlike traditional user-based licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup pay-as-you-go billing uses an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: As a first step, you should link an Azure subscription in pay-as-you-go, if you haven't already done so.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 Backup workloads have a list price of $0.15 per GiB per month of protected content.
claims.quote: The list price is $0.15/GiB/month of protected content.

claims.claim: Protected storage billing for existing workloads counts live content plus deleted and versioned data held for recovery.
claims.quote: Summation of the user-facing size of the protected content: ... Summation of the deleted and versioned data held for recovery in the backups:

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A Teams-specific backup price has not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "Backup" "channel" "pricing" "enable"; Microsoft 365 Teams channel backup message size GiB price billing. Read backup-pricing, backup-overview and backup-whats-new; none gives a Teams-specific rate.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go setup is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center, and then go to Billing > Pay-as-you-go.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go billing experience offers budget alerts.
claims.quote: To send budget spending alerts, in the Recipients box, select the name of one or more groups that you want to receive alert messages.

claims.claim: The billing setup experience can create an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: From the Subscription drop-down list, select an existing Azure subscription, or select Create a new subscription.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The new billing experience supports departmental billing and dividing backup costs among Azure subscriptions.
claims.quote: Now you can connect multiple billing policies to Backup and segment backup costs into different Azure subscriptions.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup for existing workloads is available in GCC.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup is now available for Government Community Cloud (GCC) organizations.

claims.claim: SharePoint Administrator is a documented role for setting up Microsoft 365 Backup.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator to be able to access the Microsoft 365 admin center and set up Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.claim: Global Administrator is a documented role for setting up Microsoft 365 Backup.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator to be able to access the Microsoft 365 admin center and set up Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.claim: Customers onboarded before April 2026 can migrate to the new billing experience.
claims.quote: Customers onboarded before April 1, 2026 can use Migrate to move Microsoft 365 Backup pay-as-you-go billing management from Setup or Org settings into the Billing experience in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup supports email notifications and digests for backup events.
claims.quote: Notifications are sent as a daily email digest when at least one relevant event occurs.

claims.claim: The existing backup-policy interface is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup.
claims.quote: Select Settings. Select Microsoft 365 Backup from the list of products. On the Microsoft 365 Backup page, in the SharePoint section, select Set up policy.
claims.fix: Give the full creation path: 'Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > workload > Set up policy'. Say the documented workload sections are SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange; Teams configuration is not yet documented.

claims.claim: POST /solutions/backupRestore/enable is the API equivalent of configuring workload backup policies and restore points.
claims.quote: Enable the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage service for a tenant.
claims.fix: Remove this endpoint from the policy-management row because it enables Backup Storage, not policies or restore points. If retained as a separate service-enablement row, use 'POST /v1.0/solutions/backupRestore/enable' and retain the registered-controller-app restriction.

claims.claim: The enable endpoint requires BackupRestore-Control.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | BackupRestore-Control.ReadWrite.All ... Application | BackupRestore-Control.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: A billing policy is added through Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > Add a billing policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center, and then go to Billing > Pay-as-you-go. On the Billing policies tab, select Add a billing policy.

claims.claim: No equivalent API is documented for the Microsoft 365 billing-policy and budget setup shown in this row.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup pay as you go billing policy budget alerts create API automation. Read pay-as-you-go-setup-billing-node, backup-billing and Azure Budgets Create Or Update; Azure budgets and third-party app billing are different controls.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; controls[2].api; controls[2].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Teams channel workload configuration in backup policies is not yet documented in the UI or API.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel protection policy admin center Graph API configuration. Read backup-setup, backup-view-edit-policies and Graph backup/recovery overview; documented workload policies cover SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange.

claims.claim: The arriving Teams channel backup feature is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel backup default admin opt in roles SharePoint Administrator restore destination new location. Read roadmap record, backup-setup and backup-view-edit-policies; none specifies the Teams workload's arrival default.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'unknown' and state that Microsoft has not yet specified whether existing backup policies or enablement affect Teams coverage. Existing workload setup is not proof of the new workload's default.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing setup precedes creating Microsoft 365 Backup policies.
claims.quote: 1. Set up pay-as-you-go billing ... 2. Create backup policies to protect your data ... Now that Microsoft 365 Backup is enabled for your organization, follow through to create policies and start protecting your content.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: paragraph after table
claims.claim: The cited Backup Storage API is intended for registered Backup Controller applications.
claims.quote: These APIs are intended for use by registered Backup Controller applications.

claims.claim: Departmental billing is configured in the same Backup pages as notification digests.
claims.quote: In the Services tab of Pay-as-you-go page, select Microsoft 365 Backup. To enable departmental billing, in the Settings tab of Microsoft 365 Backup page, select the checkbox for limiting management of Backup within departments.
claims.fix: Separate the paths: notifications use Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Email notifications; departmental billing uses Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Microsoft 365 Backup > Settings. Cite backup-setup and backup-billing respectively.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup consumption and meter breakdowns appear in Azure Cost Management.
claims.quote: You can view actual and accumulated cost breakdown by tenants and service type for OneDrive, SharePoint, and Exchange in Microsoft Cost Management in the Azure portal
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-billing to sources for consumption and meter reporting.

claims.claim: Existing SharePoint granular restore has a 14-day recovery-point window.
claims.quote: Granular file and folder restore is available only for recovery points within the most recent 14 days, regardless of the configured recovery window.

claims.claim: Teams-specific restore granularity and application of the SharePoint granular restore window are not established.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel protection policy admin center Graph API configuration. Opened backup-restore-data and backup-whats-new; neither documents Teams restore granularity or its recovery-point window.

claims.claim: How channel-message size will be counted for Teams backup billing is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Teams channel backup message size GiB price billing. Read backup-pricing and backup-overview; storage definitions cover existing sites, OneDrive accounts and mailboxes, not a Teams channel-message meter.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to configure email notifications, but the controls table has no corresponding row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Configure email notifications for backup events to the operations team.' Controls rows: backup policies; pay-as-you-go billing policy and budget alerts; Teams channel workload in backup policies.
claims.fix: Add an email-notification control row with Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Email notifications, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-setup#enable-email-notifications. Search its automation surface before filling the API side.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to check departmental billing, but the controls table lacks its separate setting.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Confirm your Microsoft 365 Backup billing is on the Billing > Pay-as-you-go experience ... so budget alerts and departmental billing apply.' The billing control row only gives the Add a billing policy wizard.
claims.fix: Add a departmental-billing row with Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Microsoft 365 Backup > Settings and the limiting-management checkbox, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-billing#set-up-departmental-billing. Search its automation surface separately.
